+func searchIssuesWithQuery(t *testing.T, session *TestSession, query url.Values, expectedStatus int) []*api.Issue {
+	t.Helper()

+	t.Helper()

+		Message string `json:"message"`
+	}

+	assert.NotEmpty(t, apiError.Message)
+	return apiError.Message
+}
+
+func assertIssuesOwnedBy(t *testing.T, issues []*api.Issue, owner string) {
+	t.Helper()
+	assert.NotEmpty(t, issues)
+	for _, issue := range issues {
+		if assert.NotNil(t, issue.Repo) {
+			assert.Equal(t, owner, issue.Repo.Owner)
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+func hasIssueOutsideOwner(issues []*api.Issue, owner string) bool {
+	for _, issue := range issues {
+		if issue.Repo != nil && issue.Repo.Owner != owner {
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+	return false
+}
+
+func hasIssueInRepo(issues []*api.Issue, owner, repo string) bool {
+	for _, issue := range issues {
+		if issue.Repo != nil && issue.Repo.Owner == owner && issue.Repo.Name == repo {
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+	return false
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env python
+# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
+
+import unittest
+
+from girder.utility import plugin_utilities
+
+
+class PluginUtilitiesTestCase(unittest.TestCase):
+
+    def testToposortDoesNotMutateGraphAndResolvesDependencies(self):
+        graph = {
+            'app': set(['feature']),
+            'feature': set(['core']),
+            'core': set(['core', 'external'])
+        }
+        original = dict((name, set(deps)) for name, deps in graph.items())
+
+        self.assertEqual(
+            list(plugin_utilities.toposort(graph)),
+            [set(['external']), set(['core']), set(['feature']), set(['app'])])
+        self.assertEqual(graph, original)
+
+    def testLoadPluginsResolvesClosureInDeterministicOrderAndReturnsSuccesses(self):
+        metadata = {
+            'app': {'dependencies': set(['feature', 'core'])},
+            'feature': {'dependencies': set(['core'])},
+            'core': {'dependencies': set()},
+            'independent': {'dependencies': set()}
+        }
+        loaded = []
+        old_find = plugin_utilities.findAllPlugins
+        old_load = plugin_utilities.loadPlugin
+        plugin_utilities.findAllPlugins = lambda: metadata
+
+        def load(name, root, appconf):
+            loaded.append(name)
+
+        plugin_utilities.loadPlugin = load
+        try:
+            result = plugin_utilities.loadPlugins(
+                ['app', 'independent', 'app'], object(), {})
+        finally:
+            plugin_utilities.findAllPlugins = old_find
+            plugin_utilities.loadPlugin = old_load
+
+        self.assertEqual(loaded, ['core', 'independent', 'feature', 'app'])
+        self.assertEqual(result, loaded)
+
+    def testUnknownRequestedPluginFailsBeforeLoadingAnything(self):
+        metadata = {'app': {'dependencies': set()}}
+        loaded = []
+        old_find = plugin_utilities.findAllPlugins
+        old_load = plugin_utilities.loadPlugin
+        plugin_utilities.findAllPlugins = lambda: metadata
+        plugin_utilities.loadPlugin = lambda name, root, appconf: loaded.append(name)
+        try:
+            self.assertRaises(Exception, plugin_utilities.loadPlugins,
+                              ['missing'], object(), {})
+        finally:
+            plugin_utilities.findAllPlugins = old_find
+            plugin_utilities.loadPlugin = old_load
+        self.assertEqual(loaded, [])
+
+    def testUnknownDependencyFailsBeforeLoadingAnything(self):

@@ -0,0 +1,50 @@
+; RUN: clspv-opt --passes=rewrite-packed-structs %s -o %t
+; RUN: FileCheck %s < %t
+
+; Verify that the rewrite-packed-structs transformation handles opaque-pointer
+; kernels: GEPs that index a packed-struct buffer must be lowered to operate on
+; a byte-array equivalent of the packed struct (an i8 array whose length equals
+; the struct's allocation size), while the original element index is preserved
+; and the buffer argument is still accessed directly.
+
+target datalayout = "e-p:32:32:32-i1:8:8-i8:8:8-i16:16:16-i32:32:32-i64:64:64-f32:32:32-f64:64:64-v16:16:16-v24:32:32-v32:32:32-v48:64:64-v64:64:64-v96:128:128-v128:128:128-v192:256:256-v256:256:256-v512:512:512-v1024:1024:1024"
+target triple = "spir-unknown-unknown"
+
+%struct6 = type <{ i32, i16 }>
+%struct5 = type <{ i32, i8 }>
+
+; A dynamic (global-id based) index into a 6-byte packed struct.
+; CHECK-LABEL: define spir_kernel void @test_dynamic
+; CHECK: [[gid:%[a-zA-Z0-9_.]+]] = call spir_func i32 @_Z13get_global_idj(i32 0)
+; CHECK-NOT: alloca
+; CHECK: getelementptr {{.*}}[6 x i8]{{.*}}, ptr addrspace(1) %in, i32 [[gid]]
+define spir_kernel void @test_dynamic(ptr addrspace(1) nocapture %in) {
+  %1 = call spir_func i32 @_Z13get_global_idj(i32 0)
+  %2 = getelementptr inbounds %struct6, ptr addrspace(1) %in, i32 %1
+  store %struct6 <{ i32 2100483600, i16 127 }>, ptr addrspace(1) %2, align 1
+  ret void
+}
+
+; A dynamic index into a 5-byte packed struct.
+; CHECK-LABEL: define spir_kernel void @test_dynamic5
+; CHECK: [[gid5:%[a-zA-Z0-9_.]+]] = call spir_func i32 @_Z13get_global_idj(i32 0)
+; CHECK-NOT: alloca
+; CHECK: getelementptr {{.*}}[5 x i8]{{.*}}, ptr addrspace(1) %in, i32 [[gid5]]
+define spir_kernel void @test_dynamic5(ptr addrspace(1) nocapture %in) {
+  %1 = call spir_func i32 @_Z13get_global_idj(i32 0)
+  %2 = getelementptr inbounds %struct5, ptr addrspace(1) %in, i32 %1
+  store %struct5 <{ i32 2100483600, i8 127 }>, ptr addrspace(1) %2, align 1
+  ret void

+    assert cirq.with_measurement_key_mapping(
+        object(), {'old': 'new'}, default=None) is None
+    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match='with_measurement_key_mapping'):
+        cirq.with_measurement_key_mapping(object(), {'old': 'new'})
+
+
+def test_protocol_not_implemented_fallback_and_error():
+    class ReturnsNotImplemented:
+        def _with_measurement_key_mapping_(self, key_map):
+            return NotImplemented
+
+    assert cirq.with_measurement_key_mapping(
+        ReturnsNotImplemented(), {'old': 'new'}, default='unchanged') == 'unchanged'
+    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match='with_measurement_key_mapping'):
+        cirq.with_measurement_key_mapping(

+def test_measurement_gate_mapping_is_simultaneous_and_keeps_unmapped_keys():
+    gate = cirq.MeasurementGate(2, key='a', invert_mask=(True, False))
+    mapped = cirq.with_measurement_key_mapping(gate, {'a': 'b', 'b': 'c'})
+
+    assert isinstance(mapped, cirq.MeasurementGate)
+    assert mapped.key == 'b'
+    assert cirq.with_measurement_key_mapping(
+        cirq.MeasurementGate(1, key='untouched'), {'a': 'b'}).key == 'untouched'
+
+
+def test_measurement_gate_mapping_preserves_metadata_and_source():
+    gate = cirq.MeasurementGate(2, key='a', invert_mask=(True, False))
+    mapped = cirq.with_measurement_key_mapping(gate, {'a': 'renamed'})
+
+    assert mapped.num_qubits() == 2

+    q0 = cirq.LineQubit(0)

+    assert mapped_op.gate.invert_mask == (True,)
+    non_measurement = cirq.X(q0)

+
+
+class _FakeCursor:
+    def __init__(self, rows, label):
+        self.rows = rows
+        self.label = label
+        self.calls = []
+        self.cancel_count = 0
+        self.close_count = 0
+        self.description = [(label, "varchar")]
+        self.update_type = "SELECT"
+        self.rowcount = len(rows) if rows is not None else -1
+        self.query = f"select {label}"
+        self.query_id = f"query-{label}"
+
+    def execute(self, sql, params=None):
+        self.calls.append((sql, params))
+        return "driver-result"
+
+    def fetchall(self):
+        return self.rows
+
+    def cancel(self):
+        self.cancel_count += 1
+
+    def close(self):
+        self.close_count += 1
+
+
+class _FakeHandle:
+    def __init__(self, result_sets):
+        self.result_sets = list(result_sets)
+        self.cursors = []
+        self.close_count = 0
+
+    def cursor(self):
+        rows = self.result_sets[len(self.cursors)]
+        cursor = _FakeCursor(rows, f"value_{len(self.cursors) + 1}")
+        self.cursors.append(cursor)
+        return cursor
+
+    def close(self):
+        self.close_count += 1
+
+

+        connection = ConnectionWrapper(handle, prepared_statements_enabled=True)
+
+        first = connection.cursor()
+        second = connection.cursor()
+        self.assertIsNot(first, second)
+        self.assertEqual(len(handle.cursors), 2)
+
+        first.execute("first query")
+        second.execute("second query")
+        self.assertEqual(first.fetchone(), (1,))
+        self.assertEqual(second.fetchone(), (10,))
+        self.assertEqual(first.fetchall(), [(2,)])
+        self.assertEqual(second.fetchall(), [(20,)])
+        self.assertEqual(first.description, [("value_1", "varchar")])
+        self.assertEqual(second.description, [("value_2", "varchar")])
+
+    def test_cursor_close_and_cancel_are_local_but_connection_owns_all_cursors(self):
+        handle = _FakeHandle([[('first',)], [('second',)]])

diff --git a/tests/test_usage_manager.py b/tests/test_usage_manager.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..0f050a5
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_usage_manager.py
@@ -0,0 +1,261 @@
+
+

+
+"""Tests for usage tracking and the cleanup of stale virtualenvs."""
+
+import importlib
+import os
+import pkgutil
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from datetime import datetime, timedelta
+
+import fades
+from fades import cache
+
+DATE_FORMAT = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f"
+
+
+def get_usage_manager_class():
+    """Locate the UsageManager class wherever it lives in the fades package."""
+    for _, modname, _ in pkgutil.iter_modules(fades.__path__, fades.__name__ + '.'):
+        if modname.rsplit('.', 1)[-1] == '__main__':
+            continue
+        try:
+            module = importlib.import_module(modname)
+        except Exception:
+            continue
+        cls = getattr(module, 'UsageManager', None)
+        if cls is not None:
+            return cls
+    raise AssertionError("Could not find a UsageManager class in the fades package")
+
+
+class BaseTestCase(unittest.TestCase):
+    """Common helpers."""
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.UsageManager = get_usage_manager_class()
+
+        self.basedir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="test-fades-base")
+
+        fd, self.cache_path = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix="test-fades-cache")
+        os.close(fd)
+        self.addCleanup(lambda: os.path.exists(self.cache_path) and os.remove(self.cache_path))
+
+        self.stat_path = os.path.join(self.basedir, 'usage_stats')
+        self.venvscache = cache.VEnvsCache(self.cache_path)
+
+    def make_venv(self, uuid, create_dir=True):
+        """Register a venv in the cache (and optionally create its dir on disk)."""
+        env_path = os.path.join(self.basedir, uuid)
+        if create_dir:
+            os.makedirs(env_path, exist_ok=True)
+        metadata = {
+            'env_path': env_path,
+            'env_bin_path': os.path.join(env_path, 'bin'),
+            'pip_installed': True,
+        }
+        self.venvscache.store({}, metadata, 'pythonX.Y', options={})
+        return env_path
+
+    def read_usage_lines(self):
+        with open(self.stat_path, 'rt') as fh:
+            return [line.strip() for line in fh if line.strip()]
+
+    def write_usage(self, records):
+        """Write usage records; records is a list of (uuid, datetime)."""
+        with open(self.stat_path, 'wt') as fh:
+            for uuid, when in records:
+                fh.write('{} {}\n'.format(uuid, datetime.strftime(when, DATE_FORMAT)))
+
+
+class GetVenvsMetadataTestCase(BaseTestCase):
+    """The cache exposes the metadata of every stored venv."""
+
+    def test_empty_cache(self):
+        self.assertEqual(list(self.venvscache.get_venvs_metadata()), [])
+
+    def test_yields_all_metadata(self):
+        p1 = self.make_venv('uuid-1')
+        p2 = self.make_venv('uuid-2')
+        p3 = self.make_venv('uuid-3')
+
+        result = list(self.venvscache.get_venvs_metadata())
+        env_paths = sorted(m['env_path'] for m in result)
+        self.assertEqual(env_paths, sorted([p1, p2, p3]))
+
+        by_path = {m['env_path']: m for m in result}
+        self.assertEqual(by_path[p1]['env_bin_path'], os.path.join(p1, 'bin'))
+
+
+class InitTestCase(BaseTestCase):
+    """Seeding of the usage stats file on construction."""
+
+    def test_seeds_file_when_missing(self):
+        self.make_venv('uuid-1')
+        self.make_venv('uuid-2')
+        self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(self.stat_path))
+
+        before = datetime.utcnow()
+        self.UsageManager(self.stat_path, self.venvscache)
+        after = datetime.utcnow()
+
+        self.assertTrue(os.path.exists(self.stat_path))
+        lines = self.read_usage_lines()
+        self.assertEqual(len(lines), 2)
+        seen = {}
+        for line in lines:
+            uuid, stamp = line.split()
+            seen[uuid] = datetime.strptime(stamp, DATE_FORMAT)
+        self.assertEqual(set(seen), {'uuid-1', 'uuid-2'})
+        for when in seen.values():
+            self.assertTrue(before - timedelta(seconds=5) <= when <= after + timedelta(seconds=5))
+
+    def test_seeds_empty_when_no_venvs(self):
+        self.UsageManager(self.stat_path, self.venvscache)
+        self.assertTrue(os.path.exists(self.stat_path))
+        self.assertEqual(self.read_usage_lines(), [])
+
+    def test_does_not_touch_existing_file(self):
+        self.make_venv('uuid-1')
+        old = datetime.utcnow() - timedelta(days=5)
+        self.write_usage([('some-old-uuid', old)])
+        original = self.read_usage_lines()
+
+        self.UsageManager(self.stat_path, self.venvscache)
+
+        self.assertEqual(self.read_usage_lines(), original)
+
+
+class StoreUsageStatTestCase(BaseTestCase):
+    """Recording usage appends a record."""
+
+    def test_appends_record(self):
+        env_path = self.make_venv('uuid-1')
+        manager = self.UsageManager(self.stat_path, self.venvscache)
+
+        self.assertEqual(len(self.read_usage_lines()), 1)
+
+        before = datetime.utcnow()
+        manager.store_usage_stat({'env_path': env_path})
+        after = datetime.utcnow()
+
+        lines = self.read_usage_lines()
+        self.assertEqual(len(lines), 2)
+        uuid, stamp = lines[-1].split()
+        self.assertEqual(uuid, 'uuid-1')
+        when = datetime.strptime(stamp, DATE_FORMAT)
+        self.assertTrue(before - timedelta(seconds=5) <= when <= after + timedelta(seconds=5))
+
+    def test_appends_without_dropping_others(self):
+        self.make_venv('uuid-1')
+        env_path2 = self.make_venv('uuid-2')
+        manager = self.UsageManager(self.stat_path, self.venvscache)
+        self.assertEqual(len(self.read_usage_lines()), 2)
+
+        manager.store_usage_stat({'env_path': env_path2})
+
+        lines = self.read_usage_lines()
+        uuids = [line.split()[0] for line in lines]
+        self.assertEqual(uuids.count('uuid-1'), 1)

+        'status': status,

+        'can_send_polls': True,

+    }

+    payload = {

+        'from': {'id': 100, 'first_name': 'Moderator', 'is_bot': False},
+        'date': MEMBERSHIP_TIMESTAMP,
+        'old_chat_member': _member_payload(ChatMember.MEMBER),
+        'new_chat_member': _member_payload(
+            ChatMember.RESTRICTED, can_send_messages=False, can_invite_users=True),
+    }
+    if include_invite_link:
+        payload['invite_link'] = {
+            'invite_link': 'https://t.me/joinchat/codespec',
+            'creator': {'id': 101, 'first_name': 'Inviter', 'is_bot': False},
+            'is_primary': False,
+            'is_revoked': False,
+            'expire_date': EXPIRY_TIMESTAMP,
+            'member_limit': 0,

+    return payload

+

+    assert ChatMemberHandler.__name__ == 'ChatMemberHandler'
+
+    creator = User(101, 'Inviter', False)
+    actor = User(100, 'Moderator', False)
+    chat = Chat(-10042, Chat.SUPERGROUP)
+    old_member = ChatMember(User(200, 'Target', False), ChatMember.MEMBER)
+    new_member = ChatMember(User(200, 'Target', False), ChatMember.LEFT)
+    link = ChatInviteLink('https://t.me/joinchat/direct', creator, False, False,

+    change = ChatMemberUpdated(

#!/bin/bash
set -e

cd /testbed

# Ensure Go 1.23 is used (GOPATH-era project)
export PATH="/opt/go-1.23/bin:$PATH"

# Set up GOPATH symlink so the project is importable as github.com/pingcap/tidb
export GOPATH=/root/go
export PATH="$GOPATH/bin:$PATH"
mkdir -p /root/go/src/github.com/pingcap
if [ ! -L /root/go/src/github.com/pingcap/tidb ]; then
    ln -sf /testbed /root/go/src/github.com/pingcap/tidb
fi

# Create vendor symlink (required by Makefile)
cd /root/go/src/github.com/pingcap/tidb
rm -rf vendor
ln -sf _vendor/vendor vendor

# Install parser generation tools if missing
if ! command -v goyacc &> /dev/null || ! command -v golex &> /dev/null; then
    go install github.com/qiuyesuifeng/goyacc@latest
    go install github.com/qiuyesuifeng/golex@latest
fi

# Generate parser if missing (required for build)
if [ ! -f parser/parser.go ]; then
    TEMP_FILE=temp_parser_file
    goyacc -o /dev/null -xegen "$TEMP_FILE" parser/parser.y
    goyacc -o parser/parser.go -xe "$TEMP_FILE" parser/parser.y
    rm -f "$TEMP_FILE" y.output
    golex -o parser/scanner.go parser/scanner.l
    # Fix yyEofCode -> yyEOFCode and strip //line directives
    sed -i -e 's|//line.*||' -e 's/yyEofCode/yyEOFCode/' parser/parser.go
    # Remove trailing invalid UTF-8 bytes injected by goyacc
    truncate -s -3 parser/parser.go
    printf '\n' >> parser/parser.go
    # Add "Code generated by goyacc" header
    awk 'BEGIN{print "// Code generated by goyacc"} {print $0}' parser/parser.go > tmp_parser.go && mv tmp_parser.go parser/parser.go
    awk 'BEGIN{print "// Code generated by goyacc"} {print $0}' parser/scanner.go > tmp_scanner.go && mv tmp_scanner.go parser/scanner.go
fi

# Run the TestBuiltin test from executor/executor_test.go
cd /root/go/src/github.com/pingcap/tidb/executor
GO111MODULE=off go test -v -run "TestT" -check.f "TestBuiltin"

+
+
+def _run_analyze(N, seed=100):
+    problem = read_param_file(PARAM_FILE)
+    param_values = fast_sampler.sample(problem, N=N, seed=seed)
+    Y = Ishigami.evaluate(param_values)
+    return fast.analyze(problem, Y, seed=seed)

+        assert len(Si[key]) == 3, f"expected 3 values for {key}, got {len(Si[key])}"
+
+
+def test_analyze_confidence_intervals_are_finite_and_positive_for_N_4935():
+
+    Si = _run_analyze(N=4935)
+
+    for key in ("S1_conf", "ST_conf"):
+        vals = np.asarray(Si[key], dtype=float)
+        assert np.all(np.isfinite(vals)), f"{key} contains non-finite values: {vals}"
+        assert np.all(vals > 0.0), f"{key} contains non-positive values: {vals}"
+

+

+    assert_allclose(Si["ST"], [0.55, 0.44, 0.24], atol=5e-2, rtol=1e-1)

+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from curated_transformers.generation.config import (
+    GreedyGeneratorConfig,
+    SampleGeneratorConfig,
+)
+from curated_transformers.generation.state import GeneratorState
+from curated_transformers.generation.stop_conditions import EndOfSequenceCondition
+
+
+def _state(generated_ids, batch_size=1):
+    prompt_ids = torch.arange(batch_size, dtype=torch.long).reshape(batch_size, 1)
+    state = GeneratorState(
+        attention_mask=torch.ones((batch_size, 1), dtype=torch.bool),
+        cache=None,
+        prompt_ids=prompt_ids,
+    )
+    state.generated_ids = torch.tensor(generated_ids, dtype=torch.long)
+    return state
+
+
+def _flags(batch_size=1):
+    return (
+        torch.zeros((batch_size, 1), dtype=torch.bool),
+        torch.zeros((batch_size, 1), dtype=torch.bool),
+    )
+
+
+def test_eos_condition_accepts_alias_ids_and_ignores_other_ids():
+    state = _state([[9]])
+    completed_exclude, completed_include = _flags()
+    EndOfSequenceCondition([4, 9]).update_completed(
+        state=state,
+        completed_exclude=completed_exclude,
+        completed_include=completed_include,
+    )
+    assert completed_exclude.item()
+    assert not completed_include.item()
+
+    state.generated_ids = torch.tensor([[8]], dtype=torch.long)
+    completed_exclude, completed_include = _flags()
+    EndOfSequenceCondition([4, 9]).update_completed(
+        state=state,
+        completed_exclude=completed_exclude,
+        completed_include=completed_include,
+    )
+    assert not completed_exclude.item()
+    assert not completed_include.item()
+
+    for config_cls in (GreedyGeneratorConfig, SampleGeneratorConfig):
+        state.generated_ids = torch.tensor([[9]], dtype=torch.long)
+        completed_exclude, completed_include = _flags()
+        condition = config_cls(
+            eos_id=[4, 9], max_generated_pieces=3, min_generated_pieces=0
+        ).stop_condition()
+        condition.update_completed(
+            state=state,
+            completed_exclude=completed_exclude,
+            completed_include=completed_include,
+        )
+        assert completed_exclude.item()
+
+
+def test_minimum_length_delays_eos_and_later_eos_still_stops():
+    assert GreedyGeneratorConfig(eos_id=4, max_generated_pieces=2).min_generated_pieces == 0
+    config = GreedyGeneratorConfig(
+        eos_id=[4, 9], max_generated_pieces=4, min_generated_pieces=2
+    )
+    state = _state([[]])
+    seq_ids, outputs = state.step(
+        cache=[],
+        predicted_ids=torch.tensor([[4]], dtype=torch.long),
+        stop_condition=config.stop_condition(),
+    )
+    assert seq_ids.tolist() == [0]
+    assert outputs.tolist() == [[4]]
+    assert not state.is_finished
+
+    seq_ids, outputs = state.step(
+        cache=[],
+        predicted_ids=torch.tensor([[9]], dtype=torch.long),
+        stop_condition=config.stop_condition(),
+    )
+    assert seq_ids.numel() == 0
+    assert outputs.numel() == 0
+    assert state.is_finished
+
+
+def test_maximum_length_includes_eos_and_finishes_sequence():
+    config = GreedyGeneratorConfig(eos_id=[4, 9], max_generated_pieces=2)
+    state = _state([[7]])
+    seq_ids, outputs = state.step(
+        cache=[],
+        predicted_ids=torch.tensor([[4]], dtype=torch.long),
+        stop_condition=config.stop_condition(),
+    )
+    assert seq_ids.tolist() == [0]
+    assert outputs.tolist() == [[4]]
+    assert state.is_finished
+
+
+def test_batch_eos_removes_only_matching_rows_and_preserves_ids():
+    config = GreedyGeneratorConfig(eos_id=[4, 9], max_generated_pieces=4)
+    state = _state([[1], [2]], batch_size=2)
+    seq_ids, outputs = state.step(
+        cache=[],
+        predicted_ids=torch.tensor([[9], [5]], dtype=torch.long),
+        stop_condition=config.stop_condition(),
+    )
+    assert seq_ids.tolist() == [1]
+    assert outputs.tolist() == [[5]]
+    assert state.seq_ids.tolist() == [1]
+    assert state.generated_ids.tolist() == [[2, 5]]
+
+
+def test_scalar_eos_remains_supported():
+    config = GreedyGeneratorConfig(eos_id=4, max_generated_pieces=3)
+    state = _state([[7]])
+    seq_ids, outputs = state.step(
+        cache=[],
+        predicted_ids=torch.tensor([[4]], dtype=torch.long),
+        stop_condition=config.stop_condition(),
+    )
+    assert seq_ids.numel() == 0
+    assert outputs.numel() == 0
+    assert state.is_finished
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "kwargs",
+    [
+        {"eos_id": [], "max_generated_pieces": 2},
+        {"eos_id": [4, "9"], "max_generated_pieces": 2},
+        {"eos_id": [4, 9.0], "max_generated_pieces": 2},
+        {"eos_id": [4], "max_generated_pieces": 2, "min_generated_pieces": -1},
+        {"eos_id": [4], "max_generated_pieces": 2, "min_generated_pieces": 1.5},
+        {"eos_id": [4], "max_generated_pieces": 2, "min_generated_pieces": 3},
+        {"eos_id": None, "max_generated_pieces": 2},
+        {"eos_id": 4, "max_generated_pieces": None},
+    ],
+)
+def test_invalid_stop_configuration_is_rejected(kwargs):
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        GreedyGeneratorConfig(**kwargs).stop_condition()

+
+from libsaas.executors import test_executor
+from libsaas.services import base, youtube
+
+
+V3_ROOT = 'https://www.googleapis.com/youtube/v3'
+ANALYTICS_ROOT = 'https://www.googleapis.com/youtube/analytics/v1/reports'
+
+
+class YouTubeTestCase(unittest.TestCase):
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.executor = test_executor.use()
+        self.executor.set_response(b'{}', 200, {})
+
+        self.service = youtube.YouTube('my-access-token')
+
+    def expect(self, method=None, uri=None, params=None):
+        if method is not None:
+            self.assertEqual(method, self.executor.request.method)
+        if uri is not None:
+            self.assertEqual(uri, self.executor.request.uri)
+        if params is not None:
+            self.assertEqual(params, self.executor.request.params)
+
+    def test_auth_header(self):
+        self.service.activities().get('snippet')
+        self.assertEqual(
+            'Bearer my-access-token',
+            self.executor.request.headers['Authorization'])
+
+        self.service.analytics().get('channel==MINE', 'views',
+                                     '2012-01-01', '2012-03-01')
+        self.assertEqual(
+            'Bearer my-access-token',
+            self.executor.request.headers['Authorization'])
+
+    def test_data_resources_urls(self):
+        for name in ('activities', 'channels', 'playlists',
+                     'videos', 'search'):
+            getattr(self.service, name)().get('snippet')
+            self.expect('GET', '{0}/{1}'.format(V3_ROOT, name))
+
+    def test_get_passes_params(self):
+        self.service.channels().get('snippet,statistics', id='abc',
+                                    maxResults=5)
+        self.expect('GET', '{0}/channels'.format(V3_ROOT),
+                    {'part': 'snippet,statistics', 'id': 'abc',
+                     'maxResults': 5})
+
+    def test_get_omits_unset_params(self):
+        self.service.activities().get('snippet')
+        self.expect('GET', '{0}/activities'.format(V3_ROOT),
+                    {'part': 'snippet'})
+
+    def test_get_serializes_booleans(self):
+        self.service.channels().get('snippet', mine=True)
+        self.expect('GET', '{0}/channels'.format(V3_ROOT),
+                    {'part': 'snippet', 'mine': 'true'})
+
+        self.service.activities().get('snippet', mine=False)
+        self.expect('GET', '{0}/activities'.format(V3_ROOT),
+                    {'part': 'snippet', 'mine': 'false'})
+
+    def test_data_resources_readonly(self):
+        for name in ('activities', 'channels', 'playlists',
+                     'videos', 'search'):
+            resource = getattr(self.service, name)()
+            self.assertRaises(base.MethodNotSupported, resource.create, {})
+            self.assertRaises(base.MethodNotSupported, resource.update, {})
+            self.assertRaises(base.MethodNotSupported, resource.delete)
+
+    def test_analytics_url_and_required_params(self):
+        self.service.analytics().get('channel==MINE', 'views',
+                                     '2012-01-01', '2012-03-01')
+        self.expect('GET', ANALYTICS_ROOT,
+                    {'ids': 'channel==MINE', 'metrics': 'views',
+                     'start-date': '2012-01-01', 'end-date': '2012-03-01'})
+
+    def test_analytics_translates_underscores(self):
+        self.service.analytics().get('channel==MINE', 'views',
+                                     '2012-01-01', '2012-03-01',
+                                     dimensions='day', filters='country==IT',
+                                     max_results=10, start_index=1,
+                                     sort='-views')
+        self.expect('GET', ANALYTICS_ROOT,
+                    {'ids': 'channel==MINE', 'metrics': 'views',
+                     'start-date': '2012-01-01', 'end-date': '2012-03-01',
+                     'dimensions': 'day', 'filters': 'country==IT',
+                     'max-results': 10, 'start-index': 1, 'sort': '-views'})
+
+    def test_analytics_omits_unset_params(self):
+        self.service.analytics().get('channel==MINE', 'views',
+                                     '2012-01-01', '2012-03-01',
+                                     max_results=10)
+        self.expect('GET', ANALYTICS_ROOT,
+                    {'ids': 'channel==MINE', 'metrics': 'views',
+                     'start-date': '2012-01-01', 'end-date': '2012-03-01',
+                     'max-results': 10})
+
+    def test_analytics_readonly(self):
+        analytics = self.service.analytics()
+        self.assertRaises(base.MethodNotSupported, analytics.create, {})
+        self.assertRaises(base.MethodNotSupported, analytics.update, {})
+        self.assertRaises(base.MethodNotSupported, analytics.delete)
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    unittest.main()

+from enum import Enum
+

+

+from bilibili_api.exceptions import ArgsException
+from bilibili_api.utils import network
+from bilibili_api.utils.credential import Credential
+
+
+class ReportRequestRecorder:
+    calls = []
+    responses = []
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def record_report_requests(monkeypatch):
+    ReportRequestRecorder.calls = []
+    ReportRequestRecorder.responses = []
+
+    async def fake_request(self, **kwargs):
+        if self.verify:
+            self.credential.raise_for_no_sessdata()
+        if self.method != "GET" and not self.no_csrf:
+            self.credential.raise_for_no_bili_jct()
+
+        ReportRequestRecorder.calls.append(
+            {
+                "method": self.method,
+                "url": self.url,
+                "data": dict(self.data),
+                "params": dict(self.params),
+            }
+        )
+        if ReportRequestRecorder.responses:
+            return ReportRequestRecorder.responses.pop(0)
+        return {"ok": True}
+
+
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(network.Api, "request", fake_request)
+    yield ReportRequestRecorder
+
+
+def credential_with_session():
+    return Credential(sessdata="sessdata", bili_jct="csrf-token", buvid3="buvid")
+
+
+def make_comment(resource_id, comment_id, resource_type=None, credential=None):
+    if resource_type is None:
+        resource_type = comment.CommentResourceType.VIDEO
+    return comment.Comment(
+        resource_id,
+        resource_type,
+        comment_id,
+        credential=credential or credential_with_session(),
+    )
+
+
+def submitted_payload(call):
+    return call["data"] if call["data"] else call["params"]
+
+
+REPORT_REASON_VALUES = {
+    "other": 0,
+    "spam": 1,
+    "porn": 2,
+    "spoilers": 5,
+}
+
+
+def reason_for(category):
+    return comment.ReportReason(REPORT_REASON_VALUES[category])
+
+
+def assert_payload_values(call, *expected_values):
+    payload_values = list(submitted_payload(call).values())
+    for expected_value in expected_values:
+        assert expected_value in payload_values
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_report_submits_for_this_comment_and_returns_dict(record_report_requests):
+    record_report_requests.responses = [{"ok": True, "case_id": "report-a"}]
+    cmt = make_comment(24680, 13579)
+    reason = reason_for("spam")
+
+    result = await cmt.report(reason)
+
+    assert result == {"ok": True, "case_id": "report-a"}
+    assert len(record_report_requests.calls) == 1
+    assert_payload_values(
+        record_report_requests.calls[0],
+        24680,
+        13579,
+        comment.CommentResourceType.VIDEO.value,
+        reason.value,
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_report_uses_different_comment_identity_and_reason_values(
+    record_report_requests,
+):
+    record_report_requests.responses = [
+        {"ok": True, "case_id": "one"},
+        {"ok": True, "case_id": "two"},
+    ]
+    first = make_comment(111, 222)
+    second = make_comment(333, 444)
+    spoilers_reason = reason_for("spoilers")
+    porn_reason = reason_for("porn")
+
+    first_result = await first.report(spoilers_reason)
+    second_result = await second.report(porn_reason)
+
+    assert first_result == {"ok": True, "case_id": "one"}
+    assert second_result == {"ok": True, "case_id": "two"}
+    assert len(record_report_requests.calls) == 2
+    first_payload = submitted_payload(record_report_requests.calls[0])
+    second_payload = submitted_payload(record_report_requests.calls[1])
+    assert_payload_values(record_report_requests.calls[0], 111, 222, spoilers_reason.value)
+    assert_payload_values(record_report_requests.calls[1], 333, 444, porn_reason.value)
+    assert first_payload != second_payload
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_report_preserves_non_video_comment_identity(record_report_requests):
+    record_report_requests.responses = [{"ok": True, "case_id": "article"}]
+    cmt = make_comment(
+        424242,
+        313131,
+        resource_type=comment.CommentResourceType.ARTICLE,
+    )
+    reason = reason_for("porn")
+
+    result = await cmt.report(reason)
+
+    assert result == {"ok": True, "case_id": "article"}
+    assert len(record_report_requests.calls) == 1
+    assert_payload_values(
+        record_report_requests.calls[0],
+        424242,
+        313131,
+        comment.CommentResourceType.ARTICLE.value,
+        reason.value,
+    )
+
+
+def test_enum_supports_documented_service_values():
+    assert issubclass(comment.ReportReason, Enum)
+
+    representative_reasons = [reason_for(category) for category in REPORT_REASON_VALUES]
+    assert len({reason.value for reason in representative_reasons}) == len(
+        representative_reasons
+    )
+    for reason in representative_reasons:
+        assert isinstance(reason, comment.ReportReason)
+        assert isinstance(reason.value, int)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("category", "extra_text"),
+    [
+        ("spam", "contains repeated promotion links"),
+        ("porn", "explicit screenshot reference"),

+import json

+

+import aws_sso_lib.sso as sso
+

+class StubFetcher:
+    def __init__(self, region, disable_browser):
+        self.region = region
+        self.disable_browser = disable_browser
+
+    def fetch_token(self, start_url, force_refresh=False):
+        _write_event({
+            "event": "fetch_token",
+            "region": self.region,
+            "start_url": start_url,
+            "force_refresh": force_refresh,
+        })
+
+        mode = os.environ.get("AWS_SSO_UTIL_LOGIN_STUB_MODE", "success")
+        if mode == "pending_expired":
+            raise PendingAuthorizationExpiredError()
+        if mode == "invalid_grant":
+            raise botocore.exceptions.ClientError(
+                {"Error": {"Code": "InvalidGrantException", "Message": "Device code expired"}},

+                "CreateToken",
+            )
+        if mode == "unexpected":
+            raise RuntimeError("boom")
+
+        return {"accessToken": "stub-token", "expiresAt": "2031-02-03T04:05:06Z"}
+
+
+def _write_event(event):
+    log_path = os.environ.get("AWS_SSO_UTIL_LOGIN_STUB_LOG")
+    if not log_path:
+        return
+    with open(log_path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:

+import os
+import unittest
+
+os.environ.setdefault('DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE', 'tests.test_settings')
+import django
+django.setup()
+
+from arches.app.search.elasticsearch_dsl_builder import (
+    Bool, Match, Query, Range, SimpleQueryString, Terms
+)
+
+
+class _SearchSpy(object):
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.calls = []
+
+    def search(self, **kwargs):
+        self.calls.append(kwargs)
+        return kwargs
+
+
+class DslBuilderContractTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_and_filters_are_emitted_as_an_explicit_clause(self):
+        query = Query(_SearchSpy())
+        query.add_filter(Terms(field='kind', terms='place'))
+        query.add_filter({'term': {'status': 'active'}}, operator='and')
+        query.prepare()
+        self.assertEqual(
+            query.dsl['query']['filtered']['filter'],
+            {'and': [
+                {'terms': {'kind': ['place']}},
+                {'term': {'status': 'active'}},
+            ]}
+        )
+
+    def test_or_filters_and_query_clause_coexist(self):
+        query = Query(_SearchSpy())
+        query.add_filter(Terms(field='kind', terms=['place']), operator='or')
+        query.add_filter(Terms(field='kind', terms=['building']), operator='or')
+        query.add_query(Bool(must=Match(field='name', query='museum')))
+        query.prepare()
+        self.assertEqual(
+            query.dsl['query']['filtered']['filter'],
+            {'or': [
+                {'terms': {'kind': ['place']}},
+                {'terms': {'kind': ['building']}},
+            ]}
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(query.dsl['query']['filtered']['query']['bool']['must'], [
+            {'match': {'name': {
+                'query': 'museum', 'type': 'boolean', 'operator': 'or',
+                'max_expansions': 10,
+            }}}
+        ])
+
+    def test_filter_operator_is_validated(self):
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            Query(_SearchSpy()).add_filter(Terms(field='x', terms='y'), operator='xor')
+
+    def test_bool_merge_keeps_all_three_boolean_buckets(self):
+        left = Bool(
+            must=Match(field='title', query='old'),
+            should=Terms(field='type', terms='book'),
+            must_not={'exists': {'field': 'deleted'}},
+        )
+        right = Bool(
+            must=Match(field='title', query='new'),
+            should=Terms(field='type', terms='article'),
+            must_not={'term': {'state': 'hidden'}},
+        )
+        left.merge(right)
+        self.assertEqual(len(left.dsl['bool']['must']), 2)
+        self.assertEqual(len(left.dsl['bool']['should']), 2)
+        self.assertEqual(len(left.dsl['bool']['must_not']), 2)
+        self.assertEqual(left.dsl['bool']['must_not'][1], {'term': {'state': 'hidden'}})
+
+    def test_range_preserves_zero_boost_and_rejects_conflicting_bounds(self):
+        self.assertEqual(
+            Range(field='score', gte=0, boost=0).dsl,
+            {'range': {'score': {'boost': 0, 'gte': 0}}}
+        )
+        with self.assertRaises(Exception):
+            Range(field='score')
+        with self.assertRaises(Exception):
+            Range(field='score', gte=1, gt=0)
+        with self.assertRaises(Exception):
+            Range(field='score', lte=1, lt=2)
+
+    def test_match_preserves_explicit_zero_fuzziness(self):
+        self.assertEqual(
+            Match(field='name', query='x', fuzziness=0).dsl['match']['name']['fuzziness'],
+            0
+        )
+
+    def test_simple_query_string_emits_its_declared_query_type(self):
+        self.assertEqual(
+            SimpleQueryString(
+                field=['name', 'description'], query='heritage', operator='and',
+                analyzer='standard', flags='OR|AND'
+            ).dsl,
+            {'simple_query_string': {
+                'fields': ['name', 'description'],
+                'query': 'heritage',
+                'default_operator': 'and',
+                'analyzer': 'standard',
+                'flags': 'OR|AND',
+            }}
+        )
+        scalar = SimpleQueryString(field='name', query='heritage')
+        self.assertEqual(scalar.dsl['simple_query_string']['fields'], 'name')
+
+    def test_query_search_uses_prepared_dsl_and_honors_zero_pagination(self):
+        spy = _SearchSpy()
+        query = Query(spy, start=0, limit=0, fields=[])
+        result = query.search(index='records', doc_type='resource')
+        self.assertEqual(result['body']['from'], 0)
+        self.assertEqual(result['body']['size'], 0)
+        self.assertEqual(result['body']['fields'], [])
+        self.assertEqual(result['index'], 'records')
+        self.assertEqual(result['doc_type'], 'resource')
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    unittest.main()

+
+
+import pytest
+
+from homeassistant.const import (
+    LENGTH_CENTIMETERS,
+    LENGTH_FEET,
+    LENGTH_INCHES,
+    LENGTH_KILOMETERS,
+    LENGTH_METERS,
+    LENGTH_MILES,
+    LENGTH_YARD,
+    MASS_GRAMS,
+    MASS_KILOGRAMS,
+    MASS_OUNCES,
+    MASS_POUNDS,
+    PRESSURE_BAR,
+    PRESSURE_HPA,
+    PRESSURE_PA,
+    VOLUME_FLUID_OUNCE,
+    VOLUME_GALLONS,
+    VOLUME_LITERS,
+    VOLUME_MILLILITERS,
+)
+from homeassistant.util import volume as volume_util
+from homeassistant.util import distance as distance_util
+from homeassistant.util import pressure as pressure_util
+from homeassistant.util.unit_system import IMPERIAL_SYSTEM, METRIC_SYSTEM
+
+
+def test_unit_system_mass_converts_to_metric_units():
+
+    assert METRIC_SYSTEM.mass(2.5, MASS_KILOGRAMS) == pytest.approx(2500)
+    assert METRIC_SYSTEM.mass(16, MASS_OUNCES) == pytest.approx(453.59237)
+
+
+def test_unit_system_mass_converts_to_imperial_units():
+
+    assert IMPERIAL_SYSTEM.mass(1000, MASS_GRAMS) == pytest.approx(2.20462262)
+    assert IMPERIAL_SYSTEM.mass(1, MASS_KILOGRAMS) == pytest.approx(2.20462262)
+    assert IMPERIAL_SYSTEM.mass(1, MASS_POUNDS) == 1
+
+
+def test_volume_converts_every_advertised_unit_pair():
+
+    expected_liters = {
+        VOLUME_LITERS: 1.0,
+        VOLUME_MILLILITERS: 0.001,
+        VOLUME_GALLONS: 3.785,
+        VOLUME_FLUID_OUNCE: 0.0295735,
+    }
+
+    for source, source_liters in expected_liters.items():
+        for target, target_liters in expected_liters.items():
+            result = volume_util.convert(10, source, target)
+            assert result == pytest.approx(10 * source_liters / target_liters, rel=1e-5)
+
+
+def test_distance_supports_all_advertised_units_and_round_trips():
+
+    expected_meters = {
+        LENGTH_METERS: 1.0,
+        LENGTH_KILOMETERS: 1000.0,
+        LENGTH_CENTIMETERS: 0.01,
+        LENGTH_MILES: 1609.344,
+        LENGTH_FEET: 0.3048,
+        LENGTH_INCHES: 0.0254,
+        LENGTH_YARD: 0.9144,
+    }
+    for source, source_meters in expected_meters.items():
+        converted = distance_util.convert(1, source, LENGTH_METERS)
+        assert converted == pytest.approx(source_meters, rel=1e-6)
+        assert distance_util.convert(converted, LENGTH_METERS, source) == pytest.approx(
+            1, rel=1e-6
+        )
+
+
+def test_pressure_accepts_bar_without_changing_existing_units():
+
+    assert PRESSURE_BAR in pressure_util.VALID_UNITS
+    assert pressure_util.convert(1, PRESSURE_BAR, PRESSURE_PA) == pytest.approx(100000)
+    assert pressure_util.convert(1000, PRESSURE_HPA, PRESSURE_BAR) == pytest.approx(1)
+    assert pressure_util.convert(0, PRESSURE_PA, PRESSURE_BAR) == 0
+
+
+def test_unit_system_volume_preserves_zero():
+
+    assert METRIC_SYSTEM.volume(0, VOLUME_GALLONS) == 0
+
+
+def test_measurement_converters_reject_bad_values_and_units():
+
+    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
+        METRIC_SYSTEM.mass("2", MASS_GRAMS)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        METRIC_SYSTEM.mass(2, "stones")
